claims.text: The target material is bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
The as-synthesized alloy contains inherent defects.
The proposed ML regression model incorporates measured vacancy and oxygen-impurity distributions.
The proposed ML regression model incorporates simulation-derived, temperature-dependent scattering parameters.
Quantum and defect scattering dominate electrical transport from 0 to 200 K.
Phonon and impurity scattering dominate electrical transport from 300 to 1200 K.
Oxygen contributes significantly to impurity scattering in the 300–1200 K regime.
Defects and oxygen impurities modify local electronic environments.
The presence and spatial distribution of defects and oxygen impurities modify charge-carrier scattering processes.
Explicitly representing microstructural disorder and temperature-specific scattering allows the ML model to account for non-idealities in real specimens.
The ML model can capture transitions between scattering regimes that idealized analytical models miss.
The ML model will predict electrical conductivity more accurately than analytical models that assume ideal, defect-free crystals.
The accuracy advantage will occur in both the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K intervals.
Existing analytical approaches neglect conductivity contributions from oxygen and other defects because they assume perfect, defect-free crystals.
The resulting conductivity profiles will have significantly lower prediction errors than those from traditional analytical models.
The proposed approach is limited to bulk HfNbTaTiZr specimens with approximately 1 wt.% oxygen and comparable defect structures.
Failure to produce a statistically significant reduction in conductivity-prediction error relative to traditional analytical models would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to capture the asserted change in dominant scattering mechanism between the two temperature regimes would falsify the hypothesis.
